advice: Experiment: add a 512-only B-panel packing path around the existing full512 LIBXSMM call. Before the call, pack B into column-major storage: `packed_B[j*512+k] = B[k*512+j]` for `j=0..511`, `k=0..511`. Set `parameters[4]=packed_B`, keep `parameters[10]=A` and `parameters[16]=C`, and keep all other fields zero. This presents Bᵀ directly in the column-major operand layout used by the transposed GEMM identity, while preserving every FP32 value and the existing full512 traversal. Allocate and pack inside `gemm`, include allocation and packing in timing, then free the buffer. If allocation fails, call the unchanged full512 path with the original B pointer. Hypothesis: this layout may reduce or alter the generated kernel’s B-side packing cost; the added 1 MiB allocation and full-matrix copy may outweigh any benefit. The effect is unmeasured.
risks: The proposed export is described as a no-transpose `(512,512,512)` primitive, and its body currently performs internal packing. The supplied evidence does not establish that changing only the B pointer to this column-major Bᵀ layout is compatible with that primitive’s internal B interpretation. Before benchmarking, verify the pointer/layout contract from the actual generated body or an equivalent public ABI correctness check. Check allocation failure behavior, full n=512 GEMM correctness at tolerance 0.002, general sizes and n<=0 through the unchanged fallback, and confirm the full call including packing remains timed. Do not claim a win without fresh paired controls on the block’s fixed power source and settings.
